model: DW Series duct / outside air dewpoint transmitter (BACnet MS/TP)
aliases: Greystone HTX2 high accuracy humidity transmitter
equipment_type: Duct / outdoor dewpoint and humidity sensor
applies_to: Greystone DW series duct and outside-air dewpoint transmitters (PICS models DPDDB and DPODB) and HTX2 high-accuracy RH/T transmitters with BACnet MS/TP.
summary: The DW is a Greystone duct or outside-air dewpoint transmitter with native BACnet MS/TP. It reports temperature, RH and calculated dewpoint, wet bulb and enthalpy as Analog Inputs; Analog Values hold offsets and barometric pressure/altitude, Binary Values select units, and one Multi-State Value picks what the LCD shows.
notes: Points from the object table on page 2 of the setup guide.
The object pages spell BV 1 and BV 2 as "Temperature Units" and "Enthalpy Units"; the table uses the singular.
The guide gives the default device instance as 381001 in the table and 381003 in the text; check the unit.

The HTX2 high-accuracy RH/T transmitter guide (SG-HTX2XXXBAC-001, PICS Nov 24, 2025, firmware 1.6, https://downloads.greystoneenergy.com/SG/SG-HTX2XXXBAC-001.pdf) prints the identical object list, so it is covered here.
Multistate object is MSV 1 in the guide (listed here as MV). Access from the PICS: AV, BV and MSV Present_Value are writable.

source.title: DW Series Dewpoint Transmitter - Setup Guide BACnet Communication

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP MAC and baud in the menu, set the altitude or barometric pressure for the site, then read dewpoint, temperature and RH.
setup: Device instance is 381000 + the MS/TP MAC set in the menu; it stops tracking the MAC once written over BACnet.
MS/TP baud rates 9600-115200 are supported; Max_Master defaults to 127 and is writable.
gotchas: Atmospheric Pressure and Altitude are linked; set one to match the site so the psychrometric values are right.
Enthalpy units follow the enthalpy unit BV (kJ/kg or BTU/lb); temperatures follow the temperature unit BV.

points.name: Display Mode
points.states: 1=Dew Point T, 2=Temperature, 3=Wet Bulb T, 4=RH, 5=Enthalpy, 6=T+dewpoint, 7=T+wet bulb, 8=T+RH, 9=T+enthalpy, 10=Dewpoint+wet bulb, 11=Dewpoint+RH, 12=Dewpoint+enthalpy, 13=Wet bulb+RH, 14=Wet bulb+enthalpy, 15=RH+enthalpy
